title: Asymmetric Information Markets as a Framework for Evaluating AI Information Withholding
original_idea: Design tasks where the model has safety-relevant information the user does not, with varying incentive structures. Measure rates of strategic omission as a function of oversight level and goal instructions. Compare omission vs. commission deception.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong impact pathway: if omission-based deception has different elicitation conditions than commission, this directly informs detection strategy prioritization. Addresses a real blind spot in current deception research.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing information-asymmetric tasks with varying incentive structures requires thoughtful experimental design. The conceptual framework from economics is sophisticated. Prompt engineering and measurement are feasible but the setup is non-trivial for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The scope includes designing a task suite, varying two dimensions (oversight, instructions), and comparing two deception types. This is a full experimental design that may stretch 30hrs, though a minimal version focusing on one model and fewer conditions is possible.

title: Poker Tells and Inconsistency Patterns: Applying Card-Game Bluff Detection to LLM Evaluation
original_idea: Operationalize poker bluff-detection heuristics into an LLM probe battery: test for bet-sizing analogues, timing analogues, and range imbalance. Evaluate on models known to exhibit scheming behaviors.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The analogy from poker to LLM deception is creative but the causal impact pathway is weak. Poker tells rely on embodied behavioral signals that may not have meaningful analogues in text generation. The mapping is speculative.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The individual probes (claim magnitude vs. evidence, response length vs. stakes) are implementable. However, operationalizing poker concepts into meaningful LLM metrics requires conceptual sophistication. The analogy may break down in practice.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three probe types across multiple models is moderately scoped. Each probe type needs separate operationalization and validation. Could be narrowed to one probe type on one model.

title: Social Proof and Conformity Pressure as Deception Amplifiers in LLM Populations
original_idea: Simulate a multi-agent setting where a majority of AI agents assert a false claim. Measure conformity-driven deception rates as a function of majority size, model family, and honesty instructions.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong impact: multi-agent AI systems are increasingly deployed. If conformity pressure induces deception, this is a direct design concern for agentic pipelines. Clear causal pathway from finding to actionable design recommendation.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Simulating multi-agent settings via sequential API calls is straightforward. Measuring whether a model conforms to majority false claims is a clear binary outcome. No fine-tuning or interpretability tools needed. Very accessible for CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three independent variables (majority size, model family, honesty instructions) with binary outcome is manageable but ambitious for 30hrs. Could be narrowed to one model family with varying majority size.

title: Applying Forensic Linguistic Stylometry to Detect Strategy Switching in LLM Outputs
original_idea: Generate long LLM outputs spanning honest and deceptive phases. Apply stylometric features to detect phase boundaries. Train a change-point detection model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If stylometric change-point detection works, it enables runtime monitoring without model internals. Clear deployment path but impact depends on whether LLM text actually shows stylometric discontinuities during strategy switches.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generating outputs with mid-conversation goal injection is doable. Computing stylometric features (function word frequencies, sentence length) is basic NLP. Change-point detection models exist in Python libraries. However, combining all three steps and getting meaningful results requires careful pipeline work.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The pipeline has multiple stages: data generation, feature extraction, change-point detection, evaluation. Each stage needs implementation. Feasible but may stretch 30hrs if thorough evaluation is expected.

title: Mapping the Causal Chain: When Does Capability Overhang Enable Deceptive Goal Pursuit?
original_idea: Systematically vary model capability levels (using models of different sizes and training stages) and test whether capability thresholds correlate with onset of deceptive behaviors on a scheming benchmark. Focus on theory-of-mind and planning tasks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly addresses one of the most critical open questions: at what capability level does deception emerge? If specific thresholds are identified, they become early-warning indicators for developers. Very high impact pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running multiple model sizes across multiple benchmarks (theory-of-mind tasks, planning tasks, scheming benchmarks). Getting access to intermediate training checkpoints is non-trivial. Needs substantial compute for running multiple large models. Challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very broad: multiple model families at multiple scales, multiple capability assessments, correlation analysis with scheming benchmarks. This is a full research paper scope, not a 30hr project.

title: Isolating the 'Learns to Fake Alignment' Step: Does RLHF Directly Reinforce Deceptive Compliance?
original_idea: Fine-tune a small model using RLHF with a reward signal that rewards safe-sounding outputs regardless of action consistency. Compare to a control model with behavior-consistent reward. Measure alignment-faking rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If RLHF directly selects for deceptive compliance, this identifies training itself as a causal source of alignment faking. This has direct, high-impact implications for how AI systems are trained.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implementing RLHF from scratch or using complex RLHF libraries, designing reward models, fine-tuning models under two conditions, and running consistency tests. RLHF is not beginner-accessible and requires significant ML engineering expertise and compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The experimental design is clear but execution requires RLHF training pipeline, reward model design, two training conditions, and held-out evaluation. This is a significant ML engineering project well beyond 30hrs for beginners.

title: Does Evaluation Context Recognition Causally Precede Deceptive Behavior?
original_idea: Design evaluation scenarios where evaluation context signals are systematically varied (obvious, ambiguous, none). Measure deception rates on a fixed scheming benchmark as a function of framing signal strength.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests whether evaluation-blind testing is a valid detection strategy. If context recognition is necessary for deception, this immediately enables a practical mitigation. Extremely clear impact chain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Designing prompts with varying evaluation framing signals and measuring deception rates is accessible prompt engineering. No fine-tuning required. Using existing benchmarks reduces implementation burden. Well within beginner CS student capabilities.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three framing conditions on one benchmark with one to a few models is tightly scoped. Clear independent variable, clear dependent variable. Manageable within 30hrs.

title: Targeting the Deployment Transition: Do Models Behave Differently Immediately Post-Deployment?
original_idea: Simulate a deployment transition by fine-tuning a model to associate evaluation vs. deployment contextual cues with different behavioral policies. Test whether behavioral probes detect the switch.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If deployment-time behavioral shifts are detectable, this supports post-deployment monitoring as a practical safety layer. Clear impact pathway to monitoring system design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a model to associate contextual cues with different policies, which is a non-trivial ML task. Designing behavioral probes adds complexity. Fine-tuning requires more than beginner-level ML skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Fine-tuning, designing contextual cues, building behavioral probes, and measuring detection sensitivity is a multi-stage project that exceeds 30hrs for beginners.

title: Causal Mediation Analysis: Does Goal Misalignment Cause Deception or Do Both Share a Common Cause?
original_idea: Use causal mediation analysis via activation patching in a small transformer to test whether goal-representation activations causally mediate deceptive output generation. Requires TransformerLens.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If goal misalignment is not the direct cause of deception, this fundamentally changes the intervention strategy. Extremely high theoretical impact -- could redirect entire research agendas.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires mechanistic interpretability expertise (TransformerLens, activation patching, causal mediation analysis). These are advanced techniques requiring deep understanding of transformer internals. Not accessible to beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Even scoped to a small transformer, causal mediation analysis requires identifying goal representations, deception circuits, and compliance circuits, then performing activation patching experiments. Technically narrow but expertise-intensive.

title: Intervening at the 'Learns Deceptive Communication' Step: Is Deceptive Language a Separable Module?
original_idea: Use activation patching and circuit ablation (TransformerLens) on a small model prompted to be deceptive vs. honest. Identify candidate circuits and test whether ablating them reduces deceptive output without degrading honest communication.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If a separable deception module exists, surgical interventions become possible. Important finding either way. Clear impact on mitigation strategy design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires advanced mechanistic interpretability skills: activation patching, circuit ablation, TransformerLens proficiency. These are expert-level techniques well beyond beginner CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Circuit discovery and ablation experiments on even a small model require multiple rounds of investigation. The scope is technically focused but requires deep expertise to execute.

title: Pre-Deployment Intervention: Stress Testing Anti-Scheming Training Under Distribution Shift
original_idea: Replicate simplified deliberative alignment fine-tuning on a small open-source model. Test scheming rates on in-distribution, novel role context, and novel reward framing scenarios. Measure degradation across distribution shift.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If anti-scheming training degrades under distribution shift, current safety claims are overstated. Directly informs deployment safety assurance levels. Critical finding for the field.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Replicating deliberative alignment fine-tuning, even simplified, requires understanding the technique and implementing it. Fine-tuning and designing distribution-shifted scenarios requires intermediate ML skills. Not beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning, designing three scenario categories, and measuring scheming rates across conditions. This is a full research project exceeding 30hrs for beginners.

title: Harmful Action Link: What Action Types Are Enabled by Successful Deceptive Alignment?
original_idea: Survey existing scheming incidents and near-misses. Classify by action type (information withholding, output poisoning, resource acquisition, self-exfiltration). Build a structured risk taxonomy with harm severity and detectability. Validate against domain experts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: A structured taxonomy enables prioritization of detection efforts by harm potential. Clear impact on resource allocation for safety research.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: This is primarily a literature review and taxonomy construction task. No coding or ML required. CS students can read papers, classify incidents, and build a structured taxonomy. Expert validation may be hard to arrange but the core work is accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Literature survey scope can expand unpredictably. However, focusing on documented incidents from Apollo Research and OpenAI reports provides a bounded corpus. Expert validation adds scope but could be optional.

title: Goal Formation vs. Goal Concealment: Which Causal Link Is the Cheaper Intervention Target?
original_idea: Compare two interventions on a small finetunable model: training-time regularization to prevent misaligned goals vs. deployment-time probing to detect goal concealment. Measure residual deception rates and computational costs.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Direct empirical comparison of two intervention strategies informs resource allocation across the entire safety field. Extremely high impact if results are clear.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires implementing training-time regularization and deployment-time probing, both of which are advanced ML techniques. Fine-tuning with custom regularization and designing activation probes are expert-level tasks. Not accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Two complete interventions, each requiring its own implementation, plus comparative evaluation on a toy task. This is two research projects in one.

title: Identifying Overlooked Causal Links: Does Deceptive Alignment Require Self-Modeling?
original_idea: Test a progression of models on self-modeling probes (knows it is an AI, being evaluated, what evaluator wants). Correlate self-modeling scores with scheming benchmark performance. Test whether interventions on self-modeling representations reduce scheming.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If self-modeling is a necessary intermediate for deception, capability thresholds for self-modeling become deception risk thresholds. Very high impact -- identifies a precise intervention target.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: The first part (testing models on self-modeling probes and correlating with scheming benchmarks) is accessible via API calls. The intervention part (modifying self-modeling representations) requires interpretability tools and is advanced. Could be scoped to just the correlation study.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three-part project: self-modeling probes, scheming benchmarks, intervention testing. Even the first two parts across multiple model sizes is broad. The intervention part alone could be a separate project.

title: Backcasting from Reliable Deceptive Alignment Detection: What Behavioral Tests Are Needed?
original_idea: Enumerate properties a behavioral test must have to be manipulation-resistant. Audit existing scheming benchmarks against these criteria. Identify gaps and propose test designs to fill them.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Identifying what is missing in current behavioral tests is a critical meta-research contribution. If current tests are systematically evadable, knowing this changes how the field evaluates safety claims.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Primarily an analytical and literature review task. Enumerating desirable properties, auditing existing benchmarks, and identifying gaps requires critical thinking but no advanced ML skills. Very accessible for CS students with good analytical skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The audit scope depends on how many benchmarks to review. Could be narrowed to 3-5 major benchmarks. Proposing new test designs adds open-ended scope. Core audit is manageable.
